properties.Name: Brent Spencer Bridge
properties.Description: A very important double-decker truss bridge for Kentucky & Ohio, supporting I-71 traffic both ways. The top deck is for Kentucky-bound traffic, while the bottom is for Ohio-bound. Both the top and bottom deck feature 4 compact lanes with no shoulder, making it very dangerous. I believe that currently there is federal funding for supporting a new bridge, as well as funding to change the footprint of the massive interchange north of it.

properties.Name: Quincy Street Floodwall
properties.Description: The extent of the wall itself is much longer than this, going towards downtown through Franklin Street, but this is the most striking part of it: it cuts straight down the center of the street and goes towards Bear Creek, where a small dam also is. It was first built after the Great Flood of 1937 which destroyed most of the Butchertown neighborhood that it's located in. The reason that this wall was built in the middle of the street rather than on one side or the other, is because the Army Corps of engineers wanted to avoid having to destroy the historical housing that was still standing.

properties.Name: North 10th St./Rowan St. Floodwall
properties.Description: I don't know a lot about this one, I have to do more research. I'm pretty sure all the walls were connected at some point.
